metadata.title: CRISPR Guide Sequence Design
metadata.description: Comprehensive CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA design pipeline with off-target analysis, specificity scoring, and experimental validation predictions

cells.source:
# CRISPR/Cas9 Guide RNA Design

## Objective
Design highly specific and efficient guide RNAs (gRNAs) for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing with minimal off-target effects.

## Scientific Background

### CRISPR/Cas9 System
The CRISPR/Cas9 system consists of:
- **Cas9 nuclease**: Programmable DNA endonuclease
- **Guide RNA (gRNA)**: 20-nucleotide sequence directing Cas9 to target
- **PAM sequence**: Protospacer adjacent motif (NGG for SpCas9) required adjacent to target

### Guide RNA Design Criteria

**On-target efficiency:**
- Position in gene (early exons better for knockouts)
- GC content (40-60% optimal)
- Sequence features (avoid poly-T, repeats)
- Chromatin accessibility
- Secondary structure avoidance

**Off-target specificity:**
- Genome-wide mismatch tolerance
- CFD (cutting frequency determination) score
- Position-dependent mismatch effects
- Seed region importance (8-12 bp closest to PAM)

**Experimental success factors:**
- No SNPs in target site
- Avoid repetitive regions
- Consider homopolymer runs
- Validate in relevant cell type

## This Workflow Provides
- Optimized guide designs ranked by on-target efficiency
- Comprehensive off-target analysis
- Primer design for validation
- Homology arm design for HDR
- Predicted outcomes (NHEJ, HDR efficiency)

## Input: Define Target

Specify what you want to edit.

**Options:**
1. Gene name (will find optimal cutting sites)
2. Genomic coordinates
3. DNA sequence (custom target)
4. Mutation to introduce/correct

**Customize**: Replace with your target gene or sequence.
@bioql define_target --gene TP53 --species human --genome hg38 --objective knockout --exon 5

Expected:
- Gene TP53 (tumor suppressor) identified
- Genome: Human GRCh38/hg38
- Target: Exon 5 (contains DNA binding domain)
- Genomic coordinates: chr17:7,676,154-7,676,594
- Transcript: ENST00000269305.9
- Coding sequence loaded

**Objective:** Knockout by frameshift in early functional domain

## Step 1: Find All Potential Guide Sites

Scan target region for all possible guide sequences with valid PAM.

**Cas9 variants supported:**
- SpCas9 (PAM: NGG) - most common
- SpCas9-NG (PAM: NG) - relaxed PAM
- xCas9 (PAM: NG, GAA, GAT)
- Cas12a/Cpf1 (PAM: TTTV)
- SaCas9 (PAM: NNGRRT)

**Customize**: Choose Cas9 variant based on your system.
@bioql find_guides --cas_type SpCas9 --pam NGG --region exon5 --include_strand both --min_distance_from_boundary 10

Expected: All potential guides identified

**Results:**
- 47 potential guide sequences found
- 23 on forward strand
- 24 on reverse strand
- All with valid NGG PAM
- Filtered: >10 bp from exon boundaries

**Next:** Score and rank guides by predicted performance

## Step 2: On-Target Efficiency Scoring

Predict cutting efficiency using multiple algorithms.

**Scoring methods:**
- **Doench 2016 (Rule Set 2)**: ML model trained on large dataset
- **Moreno-Mateos**: Zebrafish-trained, generalizes well
- **DeepHF**: Deep learning model for high-fidelity Cas9
- **CRISPRscan**: Position-specific scoring
- **Azimuth**: Web-based comprehensive scoring

**Customize**: Choose methods or use consensus ranking.
@bioql score_ontarget --methods doench2016,deepHF,azimuth --weights 0.4,0.3,0.3 --filter_low_scorers cutoff:0.3

Expected: Guides scored and ranked

**Top 10 guides by on-target efficiency:**

| Rank | Guide ID | Sequence (5'→3') | PAM | Doench | DeepHF | Azimuth | Consensus | GC% |
|------|----------|------------------|-----|--------|--------|---------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | TP53_E5_G12 | GGAGGAGCCGCAGTCAGATC | CGG | 0.78 | 0.82 | 0.75 | 0.78 | 60% |
| 2 | TP53_E5_G08 | CTTGCCACAGGTCTCCCCAA | GGG | 0.72 | 0.75 | 0.71 | 0.73 | 55% |
| 3 | TP53_E5_G23 | TCCCAGCTACTCCCCGCCGG | GGG | 0.70 | 0.73 | 0.68 | 0.70 | 70% |
| 4 | TP53_E5_G15 | AGTTGCAAACCAGACCTCAG | GGG | 0.68 | 0.69 | 0.66 | 0.68 | 50% |
| 5 | TP53_E5_G31 | GTCAGATCCTAGCGTCGAGC | CGG | 0.66 | 0.70 | 0.64 | 0.67 | 60% |

**Filtered out:** 12 guides with consensus score <0.3

## Step 3: Off-Target Analysis

Comprehensive genome-wide search for potential off-target sites.

**Analysis includes:**
- 0-4 mismatch tolerance
- DNA and RNA bulges
- Position-weighted scoring (seed region critical)
- CFD (Cutting Frequency Determination) scores
- Chromatin accessibility at off-targets

**Customize**: Adjust stringency based on application (research vs clinical).
@bioql analyze_offtargets --genome hg38 --mismatches 0:4 --include_bulges --score_method cfd --filter_noncoding --annotate_genes --specificity_threshold 50

Expected: Off-target analysis for top guides

**Guide: TP53_E5_G12 (Top on-target)**

**Off-target summary:**
- 0 mismatches: 1 (on-target only) ✓
- 1 mismatch: 0 ✓
- 2 mismatches: 3 (all in intergenic regions) ✓
- 3 mismatches: 47 (2 in exons, 45 intergenic)
- 4 mismatches: 234 (mostly low CFD scores)

**High-risk off-targets (CFD > 0.2):**
1. chr11:47,234,567 - 2mm (GG→AA) - Intron of MYBPC3 - CFD: 0.31
2. chr7:92,134,221 - 3mm (seed +1) - Intergenic - CFD: 0.23

**Specificity Score:** 87/100 (high specificity)

**Guide: TP53_E5_G08 (Rank 2)**

**Off-target summary:**
- 0 mismatches: 1 ✓
- 1 mismatch: 2 (both intergenic, low CFD) ⚠
- 2 mismatches: 12
- 3 mismatches: 89

**High-risk off-targets:**
1. chr9:34,567,123 - 1mm (position 15) - Intron of CDKN2A - CFD: 0.45 ⚠

**Specificity Score:** 72/100 (moderate)

**Recommendation:** G12 has better specificity than G08 despite similar on-target scores

## Step 4: Sequence Feature Analysis

Check for sequence features that may affect performance.

**Evaluated features:**
- Homopolymer runs (≥4 identical bases)
- Secondary structure (gRNA folding)
- GC content distribution
- Microsatellite repeats
- Common SNPs in target site

**Customize**: Adjust thresholds based on your tolerance.
@bioql check_sequence_features --check_snps dbSNP155 --check_repeats --secondary_structure --homopolymers max:4 --flag_issues

Expected: Feature analysis results

**Guide TP53_E5_G12:**
- Homopolymers: None ✓
- GC content: 60% (optimal) ✓
- Secondary structure: ΔG = -2.1 kcal/mol (minimal) ✓
- Common SNPs (MAF >1%): None ✓
- Repeats: None ✓
- **Overall: PASS - No issues detected**

**Guide TP53_E5_G08:**
- Homopolymers: CCCC at positions 12-15 ⚠
- GC content: 55% ✓
- Secondary structure: ΔG = -1.8 kcal/mol ✓
- SNPs: rs1234567 (MAF 2.3%) at position 18 ⚠
- **Overall: CAUTION - Poly-C stretch and SNP may affect efficiency**

## Step 5: Multi-Parameter Ranking

Combine all criteria to select best guides.

**Scoring components:**
- On-target efficiency (40%)
- Off-target specificity (40%)
- Sequence features (10%)
- Position in gene (10%)

**Customize**: Adjust weights based on priorities.
@bioql rank_guides --criteria ontarget:0.4,specificity:0.4,features:0.1,position:0.1 --select_top 5 --diversity_filter 50bp

Expected: Final ranked guide list

**Top 5 Recommended Guides:**

| Rank | Guide | Sequence | Position | Ontarget | Specificity | Features | Overall |
|------|-------|----------|----------|----------|-------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | TP53_E5_G12 | GGAGGAGCCGCAGTCAGATC | chr17:7,676,234 | 0.78 | 0.87 | 1.0 | 0.85 |
| 2 | TP53_E5_G31 | GTCAGATCCTAGCGTCGAGC | chr17:7,676,305 | 0.67 | 0.91 | 1.0 | 0.81 |
| 3 | TP53_E5_G23 | TCCCAGCTACTCCCCGCCGG | chr17:7,676,278 | 0.70 | 0.82 | 0.9 | 0.78 |
| 4 | TP53_E5_G15 | AGTTGCAAACCAGACCTCAG | chr17:7,676,256 | 0.68 | 0.85 | 0.95 | 0.77 |
| 5 | TP53_E5_G08 | CTTGCCACAGGTCTCCCCAA | chr17:7,676,198 | 0.73 | 0.72 | 0.75 | 0.73 |

**Recommendation:** Test guides 1, 2, and 3 experimentally

**Expected outcomes:**
- All three should produce indels
- G12 likely highest efficiency
- G31 highest specificity
- G23 good balance

## Step 6: Design Oligonucleotides

Generate oligo sequences for cloning into expression vectors.

**Vector options:**
- pSpCas9(BB)-2A-GFP (PX458)
- pSpCas9(BB)-2A-Puro (PX459)
- pLentiCRISPR v2
- Custom vector

**Customize**: Specify your vector and overhangs.
@bioql design_oligos --guides top_3 --vector px459 --overhangs_forward CACCG --overhangs_reverse AAAC --phosphorylate_5prime --output_format idtorder

Expected: Cloning oligos ready to order

**Guide 1 (TP53_E5_G12):**
- Forward: 5'-CACCG**GGAGGAGCCGCAGTCAGATC**-3'
- Reverse: 5'-AAAC**GATCTGACTGCGGCTCCTCC**-3'
- Length: 25 bp + overhangs
- Tm: 72°C
- Desalt purification recommended

**Guide 2 (TP53_E5_G31):**
- Forward: 5'-CACCG**GTCAGATCCTAGCGTCGAGC**-3'
- Reverse: 5'-AAAC**GCTCGACGCTAGGATCTGAC**-3'

**Guide 3 (TP53_E5_G23):**
- Forward: 5'-CACCG**TCCCAGCTACTCCCCGCCGG**-3'
- Reverse: 5'-AAAC**CCGGCGGGGAGTAGCTGGGA**-3'

**IDT Order format exported:** guides_for_ordering.xlsx

**Cloning protocol:**
1. Anneal complementary oligos (95°C → 25°C)
2. Digest pX459 with BbsI
3. Ligate annealed oligos into vector
4. Transform and verify by sequencing

## Step 7: Validation Primer Design

Design primers for PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing to validate editing.

**Primer requirements:**
- Flank target site (250-500 bp amplicon)
- Avoid primer sites with common SNPs
- Tm 58-62°C
- GC content 40-60%
- Compatible with Sanger sequencing

**Customize**: Adjust amplicon size based on needs.
@bioql design_primers --purpose validation --amplicon_size 400-500 --primers_distance_from_cut 150-200 --tm_range 58:62 --avoid_snps --output_format benchling

Expected: Validation primer pairs

**Primer Set for TP53 Exon 5 Editing:**

**Forward Primer (TP53_E5_Val_F):**
- Sequence: 5'-TCCCAAGCAATGGATGATTTGA-3'
- Position: chr17:7,676,084 (150 bp upstream of G12)
- Length: 22 bp
- Tm: 60.2°C
- GC: 45%

**Reverse Primer (TP53_E5_Val_R):**
- Sequence: 5'-TGGAGGAGCCACAAGTCTGT-3'
- Position: chr17:7,676,530 (180 bp downstream)
- Length: 20 bp
- Tm: 59.8°C
- GC: 55%

**Amplicon:**
- Size: 446 bp
- Cut site: 234 bp from 5' end (good for sequencing)
- No SNPs in primer binding sites ✓

**Sequencing Primer (uses Forward primer):**
Sequence from 5' end will reveal indels clearly

**Protocol:**
1. PCR amplify edited region
2. Run on gel to check amplicon size
3. Sanger sequence with forward primer
4. Analyze chromatogram for double peaks (indels)

## Step 8: Predict Editing Outcomes

Predict likely indel patterns and consequences.

**Analysis:**
- Microhomology-mediated deletions
- Frequency of different indel sizes
- Frameshift vs in-frame predictions
- Protein consequences

**Models used:**
- inDelphi: Deep learning indel prediction
- FORECasT: Frameshift frequency
- Lindel: Microhomology-based prediction

**Customize**: Choose model based on cell type data availability.
@bioql predict_outcomes --guide TP53_E5_G12 --model indelphi --cell_type HEK293T --top_outcomes 10 --translate_frame

Expected: Predicted editing outcomes

**Predicted Indel Spectrum (Top 10):**

| Rank | Indel | Frequency | Type | Frame | Protein Effect |
|------|-------|-----------|------|-------|----------------|
| 1 | +1 A | 24% | Insertion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +15 aa |
| 2 | Δ1 | 18% | Deletion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +22 aa |
| 3 | Δ3 | 12% | Deletion | 0 | In-frame, Δ1 aa (may retain function) |
| 4 | +1 T | 11% | Insertion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +15 aa |
| 5 | Δ7 | 8% | Deletion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +8 aa |
| 6 | Δ2 | 7% | Deletion | +1 | Frameshift → PTC at +35 aa |
| 7 | Δ9 | 5% | Deletion | 0 | In-frame, Δ3 aa |
| 8 | Δ11 | 4% | Deletion | +1 | Frameshift → PTC at +12 aa |
| 9 | +1 G | 3% | Insertion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +15 aa |
| 10 | Δ4 | 3% | Deletion | -1 | Frameshift → PTC at +18 aa |

**Summary:**
- **Frameshift indels: 77%** (desired for knockout)
- **In-frame indels: 17%** (may retain partial function)
- **WT: ~6%** (no editing or precise HDR)

**Protein prediction:**
- Most frameshifts introduce premature termination codons (PTC)
- mRNA likely degraded by nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)
- Expected result: Loss of TP53 protein (knockout)

**Interpretation:** This guide is excellent for knockout (high frameshift rate)

## Step 9: HDR Template Design (Optional)

If performing knock-in or precise correction, design homology-directed repair template.

**Template types:**
- ssODN (single-strand oligonucleotide, <200 bp)
- dsDNA donor (plasmid or PCR product)
- AAV vector (for in vivo)

**Design parameters:**
- Homology arm length (40-90 bp for ssODN, 500-1000 bp for dsDNA)
- Silent mutations to prevent re-cutting
- Orientation (sense vs antisense for ssODN)

**Customize**: Skip if doing knockout only.
@bioql design_hdr_template --guide TP53_E5_G12 --template_type ssODN --homology_arms 60bp --edit_type point_mutation --mutation R175H --block_recut --strand antisense

Expected: HDR donor template design

**HDR Template (ssODN) for R175H Mutation:**

**Target:** Introduce R175H hotspot mutation (CGC → CAC)

**Template sequence (180 bp total):**
```
5'-[60 bp left homology]---[EDIT + PAM disruption]---[60 bp right homology]-3'

5'-TCACTTGTGCCCTGACTTTCAACTCTGTCTCCTTCCTCTTCCTACAGTACTCCCCTGCCCTCAAC
   AAGATGTTTTGCCAACTGGCC**CAC**GAGACGCCTCACATCCTCACCATCATCACACTGGAAGAC
   TCCAGTGGGAACCTTCTGGGACGGGACAGCTTTGAGGTGCGTGTTTGTGCCTGTCCTGGGAGAG-3'
```

**Key features:**
- Mutation: CG**C** → CA**C** (R175H)
- Silent PAM disruption: C**CGG** → C**TGG** (prevents re-cutting)
- Additional silent mutations at positions +3, +6 to increase HDR over NHEJ
- Antisense strand (better HDR efficiency)
- Total length: 180 nt (within ssODN optimal range)

**Expected HDR efficiency:** 5-15% (typical for ssODN)

**Controls needed:**
- Guide without donor (NHEJ only)
- Donor without guide (no editing)
- Untreated cells

**Analysis:**
- PCR + Sanger sequencing (R175H = HindIII site loss)
- Restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP)
- NGS for precise quantification

## Step 10: Delivery Strategy Recommendations

Optimal delivery method based on cell type and application.

**Delivery formats:**
- Plasmid (transient expression)
- mRNA + synthetic gRNA (RNP)
- Lentiviral (stable expression)
- AAV (in vivo)
- Electroporation (RNP or plasmid)

**Customize**: Specify your cell type.
@bioql recommend_delivery --cell_type HEK293T --application knockout --duration transient --optimize_for efficiency

Expected: Delivery recommendations

**Recommended Method: RNP Electroporation**

**Rationale:**
- HEK293T are easily transfectable
- RNP = fastest editing kinetics (minutes vs hours)
- Lower off-target activity (transient presence)
- No plasmid integration concerns

**Protocol:**
1. **Prepare RNP:**
   - Cas9 protein: 1 μg (61 pmol)
   - gRNA: 120 ng (60 pmol)
   - Molar ratio 1:1
   - Incubate 10 min at RT

2. **Electroporation:**
   - 200,000 cells in 20 μL
   - Neon system: 1400V, 20ms, 2 pulses
   - Or Lonza 4D: Program CA-137

3. **Recovery:**
   - Plate in antibiotic-free media
   - Incubate 48-72h before analysis

**Expected Results:**
- Editing efficiency: 60-80%
- Cell viability: >85%
- Clonal isolation ready after 7 days

**Alternative (cheaper but lower efficiency): Plasmid Transfection**
- Use Lipofectamine 3000 or PEI
- 2 μg pX459 plasmid
- Puromycin selection (1 μg/mL, 48h)
- Expected efficiency: 40-60%

## Step 11: Experimental Timeline & Checklist

Complete workflow from design to validation.

**Customize**: Adjust timeline for your specific project.
@bioql generate_protocol --guides selected_guides --include_timeline --include_materials --include_controls --format pdf

Expected: Comprehensive experimental protocol

## Experimental Timeline (3-4 weeks)

### Week 1: Preparation
- **Day 1-2:** Order oligos and primers (IDT, 2-day delivery)
- **Day 3:** Receive and resuspend oligos
- **Day 4:** Anneal oligos, digest vector, ligate
- **Day 5:** Transform, mini-prep 3 colonies per guide
- **Day 6-7:** Sanger sequence to verify inserts

### Week 2: Transfection & Editing
- **Day 8:** Seed cells for transfection
- **Day 9:** Transfect with validated guide plasmids
- **Day 10-11:** Incubate, add selection if using puromycin
- **Day 12:** Remove selection, expand cells
- **Day 13-14:** Expand edited pool

### Week 3: Analysis
- **Day 15:** Harvest cells, extract genomic DNA
- **Day 16:** PCR amplify target region
- **Day 17:** Run gel, purify PCR products
- **Day 18:** Send for Sanger sequencing
- **Day 19:** Receive sequences, analyze TIDE or ICE
- **Day 20-21:** NGS if needed for detailed analysis

### Week 4: Clonal Isolation (if needed)
- **Day 22:** Single-cell sort or limiting dilution
- **Day 23-28:** Expand clones (7-10 days)
- **Day 29-30:** Screen clones by PCR + sequencing

## Materials Needed

**Molecular Biology:**
- [ ] Guide oligos (ordered)
- [ ] pX459 or other CRISPR vector
- [ ] BbsI restriction enzyme

**Cell Culture:**

## Controls

**Essential:**
1. Untransfected cells (negative control)
2. Empty vector or non-targeting guide (transfection control)
3. Known working guide (positive control)

**Optional:**
4. Multiple independent guide RNAs (validates phenotype)
5. Rescue experiment (re-express WT gene)

## Step 12: Analysis of Results

After experiments, analyze editing efficiency.

**Analysis methods:**
- TIDE (Tracking of Indels by Decomposition)
- ICE (Inference of CRISPR Edits)
- NGS (Next-generation sequencing - most accurate)
- Sanger + manual inspection

**Customize**: Upload your Sanger data for analysis.
@bioql analyze_editing --method TIDE --control_trace WT_sequence.ab1 --edited_traces edited_*.ab1 --guide_location 234 --calculate_frameshift

Expected: Editing efficiency results

**TIDE Analysis Results:**

**Guide 1 (TP53_E5_G12):**
- Editing efficiency: 72%
- Frameshift indels: 68%
- In-frame indels: 4%
- Wild-type: 28%
- Most common indel: +1A (28%), Δ1 (22%), Δ3 (8%)
- **Conclusion: Excellent knockout efficiency**

**Guide 2 (TP53_E5_G31):**
- Editing efficiency: 58%
- Frameshift indels: 54%
- In-frame indels: 4%
- Wild-type: 42%
- **Conclusion: Good efficiency, high specificity maintained**

**Guide 3 (TP53_E5_G23):**
- Editing efficiency: 45%
- Frameshift indels: 41%
- In-frame indels: 4%
- Wild-type: 55%
- **Conclusion: Moderate efficiency**

**Recommendation:** Use Guide 1 (G12) for further experiments

**Next steps:**
- Isolate single-cell clones
- Screen ~20 clones by PCR + sequencing
- Identify homozygous knockouts (typically 10-30% of clones)
- Validate protein knockout by Western blot

## Advanced: Multiplex CRISPR Design

Design guides for simultaneous editing of multiple targets.

**Applications:**
- Large deletions (2 guides flanking region)
- Multi-gene knockouts
- Complex genomic rearrangements

**Customize**: Add additional targets if needed.
@bioql design_multiplex --targets TP53:exon5,MDM2:exon3 --ensure_compatibility --avoid_guide_interactions --optimize_order

Expected: Compatible guide pairs for multiplexing

**Multiplex Design: TP53 + MDM2 Knockout**

**Selected Guides:**
1. TP53_E5_G12 (from above)
2. MDM2_E3_G05: GAAGAAGCTCGTTGCACGCT (CGG)

**Compatibility Analysis:**
- No sequence similarity (prevents cross-reactivity) ✓
- Different PAM locations (reduces competition) ✓
- No predicted guide-guide interactions ✓
- Similar predicted efficiencies (balanced editing) ✓

**Delivery:**
- Clone both guides into dual-guide vector (pX462)
- Or deliver as two separate plasmids (50:50 ratio)
- Or RNP with both guides simultaneously

**Expected:**
- Double-edited cells: 30-50% (TP53⁻/⁻ MDM2⁻/⁻)
- Single-edited: 20-30% each
- Unedited: 10-20%

**Screening:**
- PCR both loci simultaneously
- Sanger sequence or NGS
- Confirm genotype of clones

## Troubleshooting & Optimization

### Low Editing Efficiency (<20%)

**Possible causes:**
1. Poor guide design → Try alternative guides
2. Low transfection efficiency → Optimize delivery method
3. Cell type resistant → Try RNP electroporation
4. Chromatin accessibility → Add HDAC inhibitors

### High Off-Target Activity

**Solutions:**
1. Use high-fidelity Cas9 variants (SpCas9-HF1, eSpCas9)
2. Reduce Cas9/gRNA concentration
3. Truncated guides (17-18 nt instead of 20 nt)
4. Deliver as RNP (faster clearance)

### Biallelic Editing Needed but Getting Monoallelic

**Solutions:**
1. Increase Cas9/gRNA dose
2. Extend incubation time before clonal isolation
3. Screen more clones (binomial distribution)
4. Use mRNA/RNP for faster kinetics

### Want Knock-in but Getting Mostly NHEJ

**Solutions:**
1. Use longer homology arms (90 bp ssODN or dsDNA donor)
2. Add cell cycle modifiers (RS-1, L755507)
3. Inhibit NHEJ (SCR7, DNA Ligase IV inhibitors)
4. Time delivery to S/G2 phase
5. Use Cas9 nickase (D10A) + paired guides
